summary.en: The Founder received the abdication and took the throne

units.zh: 楊師厚，潁州斤溝人也。
units.en: Yang Shihou came from Jingou in Yingzhou.
units.literal: Yang Shihou, a man of Jingou in Yingzhou.

units.zh: 為李罕之部將，以猛決聞，尤善騎射。
units.en: A general under Li Hanzhi, he was known for boldness in battle and was an expert horse archer.
units.literal: He was a subordinate general of Li Hanzhi, famed for fierce resolve, and especially skilled at mounted archery.

units.zh: 及罕之敗，退保澤州，師厚與李鐸、何絪等來降，太祖署為忠武軍牙將，繼曆軍職，累遷檢校右僕射，表授曹州刺史。
units.en: After Hanzhi's defeat and retreat to Zezhou, Shihou surrendered with Li Duo, He Yin, and others; the Founder made him a Zhongwu staff officer, and he rose through the ranks to acting Right Vice Director and governor of Cao.
units.literal: When Hanzhi was defeated and withdrew to hold Zezhou, Shihou with Li Duo, He Yin, and others came surrendering; the Founder appointed him a junior general of the Zhongwu army; he continued through military posts, rising in repeated promotions to acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was memorialized as prefect of Cao.

units.zh: 唐天復三年，從太祖迎昭宗於岐下，李茂貞以勁兵出戰，為師厚所敗。
units.en: In Tianfu 3 he joined the Founder in bringing Emperor Zhaozong back from Qi; Li Maozhen marched out with elite troops and Shihou routed him.
units.literal: Tang Tianfu year 3, he followed the Founder to welcome Emperor Zhaozong below Qi; Li Maozhen led crack troops out to fight and was defeated by Shihou.

units.zh: 及王師範以青州叛，太祖遣師厚率兵東討，時淮賊王景仁以眾二萬來援師範，師厚逆擊，破之，追至輔唐縣，斬數百級，授齊州刺史。
units.en: When Wang Shifan rose at Qingzhou, the Founder sent Shihou east; Wang Jingren of the Huai came with twenty thousand to relieve Shifan; Shihou met him, shattered his force, pursued to Futang, took hundreds of heads, and received Qi prefecture.
units.literal: When Wang Shifan rebelled at Qingzhou, the Founder sent Shihou east with troops; at that time the Huai bandit Wang Jingren came with twenty thousand men to aid Shifan; Shihou met and struck them, broke them, pursued to Futang county, beheaded several hundred, and was appointed prefect of Qi.

units.zh: 將之任，太祖急召見於鄆西境，遣師厚率步騎屯於臨朐，而聲言欲東援密州，留輜重於臨朐。
units.en: Before he could take office the Founder called him urgently to Yan's western border, posted him at Linqu with foot and horse, announced a march to relieve Mizhou, and left the baggage train there.
units.literal: As he was about to take up the post, the Founder urgently summoned him to the western border of Yan, sent Shihou to lead infantry and cavalry to camp at Linqu, and publicly announced that he meant to march east to relieve Mizhou, leaving baggage at Linqu.

units.zh: 師範果出兵來擊，師厚設伏於野，追擊至聖王山，殺萬餘眾，擒都將八十人。
units.en: Shifan did march out; Shihou laid an ambush, chased the enemy to Shengwang Mountain, killed over ten thousand, and took eighty officers.
units.literal: Shifan indeed sent troops to attack; Shihou set an ambush in the field, pursued to Shengwang Mountain, killed more than ten thousand, and captured eighty commanders.

units.zh: 未幾，萊州刺史王師誨以兵救師範，又大敗之。
units.en: Soon Laizhou prefect Wang Shihui came to Shifan's aid and was beaten again.
units.literal: Before long Laizhou prefect Wang Shihui led troops to rescue Shifan, and Shihou again inflicted a great defeat.

units.zh: 自是，師範不復敢戰。
units.en: After that Shifan would not fight again.
units.literal: From then on Shifan no longer dared give battle.

units.zh: 師厚移軍寨於城下，師範力屈，竟降。
units.en: Shihou shifted his camp under the walls; Shifan, exhausted, submitted at last.
units.literal: Shihou moved his camp below the city; Shifan's strength gave way and he finally surrendered.

units.zh: 天復四年三月，加檢校司徒、徐州節度使。
units.en: In the third month of Tianfu 4 he was made acting Minister of Works and commissioner of Xuzhou.
units.literal: Tianfu year 4, third month, he was advanced to acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 天祐元年，加諸軍行營馬步都指揮使。
units.en: In Tianyou 1 he was named supreme field commander of horse and foot for all armies.
units.literal: Tianyou year 1, he was advanced to overall commander of all armies' horse and foot in the field.

units.zh: 二年八月，太祖討趙匡凝於襄陽，命師厚統前軍以進，趙匡凝嚴兵以備。
units.en: In the eighth month of year 2 the Founder attacked Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and put Shihou at the head of the advance; Kuangning drew up in full strength.
units.literal: Year 2, eighth month, the Founder campaigned against Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and ordered Shihou to lead the vanguard forward; Zhao Kuangning arrayed his troops in readiness.

units.zh: 師厚至穀城西童山，刊材造浮橋，引軍過漢水。
units.en: Shihou reached Tongshan west of Gucheng, cut timber for a pontoon bridge, and crossed the Han with his men.
units.literal: Shihou reached Tongshan west of Gucheng, felled timber to build a pontoon bridge, and led the army across the Han.

units.zh: 一戰，趙匡凝敗散，攜妻子沿漢遁去。
units.en: One engagement broke Kuangning's army; he fled down the Han with his family.
units.literal: In one battle Zhao Kuangning was routed and scattered; he took wife and children and fled along the Han.

units.zh: 翌日，表師厚為山南東道節度留後。
units.en: Next day he was memorialized acting commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
units.literal: The next day Shihou was memorialized as acting military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：天祐三年六月甲申，敕：「襄州近因趙匡凝作帥，請別立忠義軍額，既非往製，固是縱權，忠義軍額宜停廢，依舊為山南東道節度使。」）〉
units.en: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 records that on jiashen in the sixth month of Tianyou 3 an edict declared: "Because Zhao Kuangning lately became commander at Xiangzhou and sought a separate Loyal and Righteous Army commission—neither the former institution nor anything but usurped authority—the Loyal and Righteous Army title should be abolished and Xiang restored to the Shannan East Circuit military commissioner.")
units.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 says: Tianyou year 3, sixth month, day jiashen, an edict: "Xiangzhou lately, because Zhao Kuangning became commander, asked to establish separately the title of the Loyal and Righteous Army; this is neither the former system nor anything but usurped authority—the Loyal and Righteous Army title should be abolished and the former Shannan East Circuit military commissioner restored.")

units.zh: 即令南討荊州，留後趙匡明亦棄軍上峽，不浹旬，並下兩鎮，乃正授襄州節度使。
units.en: He was sent south on Jingzhou; acting commander Zhao Kuangming fled up the Yangzi gorges; within ten days both commands fell, and Shihou received full appointment at Xiang.
units.literal: He was at once ordered south against Jingzhou; the acting commander Zhao Kuangming also abandoned his army and went up the gorges; within ten days both posts were taken, and Shihou was then formally appointed military commissioner of Xiang.

units.zh: 先是，漢南無羅城，師厚始興板築，周十餘里，郛郭完壯。
units.en: The Han south had lacked a city wall until Shihou built plank defenses for more than ten li and made the suburbs strong.
units.literal: Earlier in the Han south there had been no outer wall; Shihou first raised plank ramparts more than ten li around, and the suburbs stood complete and strong.

units.zh: 開平元年，加檢校太保、同平章事。
units.en: In Kaiping 1 he was made acting Grand Guardian and given co-equal ministerial rank.
units.literal: Kaiping year 1, he was advanced to acting Grand Guardian and co-equal to the chief ministers.

units.zh: 明年，又加檢校太傅。
units.en: The following year he rose to acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: The next year he was again advanced to acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 三年三月，入朝，詔兼潞州行營都招討使。
units.en: In the third month of year 3 he came to court and was named overall commander for the Lu expedition.
units.literal: Year 3, third month, he entered court; an edict also made him overall commander for the Lu campaign.

units.zh: 無何，劉知俊據同州叛，師厚與劉鄩率軍西討，至潼關，擒知俊弟知浣以獻。
units.en: Soon Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; Shihou and Liu Yan marched west, took his brother Zhihuan at Tong Pass, and sent him up.
units.literal: Before long Liu Zhijun held Tongzhou in rebellion; Shihou with Liu Yan led troops west; reaching Tong Pass they captured Zhijun's younger brother Zhihuan and presented him.

units.zh: 知俊聞師厚至，即西走鳳翔，師厚進攻，至長安。
units.en: Zhijun fled west to Fengxiang when he heard Shihou was coming; Shihou drove on to Chang'an.
units.literal: Hearing Shihou had come, Zhijun at once fled west to Fengxiang; Shihou pressed the attack to Chang'an.

units.zh: 時知俊已引岐寇據其城，師厚以奇兵傍南山急行，自西門而入，賊將王建驚愕，不知所為，遽出降。
units.en: Zhijun had already brought Qi forces into the city; Shihou raced picked men along the southern hills, burst in the west gate, and rebel commander Wang Jian, stunned, surrendered at once.
units.literal: By then Zhijun had already led Qi raiders to hold the city; Shihou with picked troops hurried along the southern hills, entered by the west gate, and the rebel commander Wang Jian, startled and at a loss, promptly came out and surrendered.

units.zh: 製加師厚檢校太尉。
units.en: He was promoted to acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: An edict advanced Shihou to acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 頃之，晉王與周德威、丁會、符存審等以大眾攻晉州甚急，太祖遣師厚帥兵援之。
units.en: Soon the Prince of Jin, Zhou Dewei, Ding Hui, Fu Cunshen, and others besieged Jinzhou fiercely; the Founder sent Shihou to the rescue.
units.literal: Before long the Prince of Jin with Zhou Dewei, Ding Hui, Fu Cunshen, and others with a great host pressed Jinzhou very hard; the Founder sent Shihou to relieve it with troops.

units.zh: 軍至絳州，晉軍扼蒙坑之險，師厚整眾而前，晉人乃徹圍而遁。
units.en: At Jiangzhou the Jin held Mengkeng Pass; Shihou formed line and marched forward, and the Jin broke off and withdrew.
units.literal: When the army reached Jiangzhou, Jin troops held the defile of Mengkeng; Shihou arrayed his host and advanced, and the Jin men then lifted the siege and fled.

units.zh: 四年二月，移授陝州節度使。
units.en: In the second month of year 4 he was transferred to Shan circuit.
units.literal: Year 4, second month, he was transferred as military commissioner of Shan.

units.zh: 五年正月，王景仁敗於柏鄉，晉人乘勝圍邢州，掠魏博，南至黎陽。
units.en: In the first month of year 5 Wang Jingren fell at Baixiang; the Jin swept on, besieged Xing, plundered Weibo, and reached Liyang.
units.literal: Year 5, first month, Wang Jingren was defeated at Baixiang; Jin men pressed the victory, besieged Xingzhou, raided Weibo, and came south to Liyang.

units.zh: 師厚受詔以兵屯衛州，晉軍攻魏州，不克而退；
units.en: Shihou was ordered to Weizhou; the Jin assaulted Wei, failed, and pulled back;
units.literal: Shihou received orders to camp at Weizhou with troops; the Jin army attacked Weizhou, could not take it, and withdrew;

units.zh: 師厚追襲，過漳河，解邢州之圍，改授滑州節度使。
units.en: Shihou chased them over the Zhang, broke the siege of Xing, and was made commissioner of Hua.
units.literal: Shihou pursued, crossed the Zhang River, lifted the siege of Xing, and was changed to military commissioner of Hua.

units.zh: 明年，太祖北征，令師厚以大軍攻棗強，逾旬不能克，太祖屢加督責，師厚晝夜奮擊，乃破之，盡屠其城。
units.en: Next year on the northern campaign the Founder ordered Shihou against Zaoqiang; for ten days the city held; the Founder drove him hard; Shihou stormed day and night, took it, and put every soul to the sword.
units.literal: The next year the Founder campaigned north and ordered Shihou with the main army to attack Zaoqiang; for more than ten days he could not take it; the Founder repeatedly pressed him; Shihou fought day and night and then broke it, slaughtering the whole city.

units.zh: 車駕還，師厚屯魏州。
units.en: When the emperor returned, Shihou remained at Wei.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Shihou camped at Weizhou.

units.zh: 及庶人友珪篡位，魏州衙內都指揮使潘晏與大將臧延範、趙訓謀變，有密告者，師厚布兵擒捕，斬之。
units.en: After Yougui seized the throne, Weizhou commander Pan Yan and generals Zang Yanfan and Zhao Xun plotted revolt; Shihou learned of it, seized them, and executed them.
units.literal: When the deposed emperor Yougui usurped the throne, Weizhou yamen commander Pan Yan with great generals Zang Yanfan and Zhao Xun plotted mutiny; an informer came forward; Shihou deployed troops, seized them, and beheaded them.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：師厚乘間殺魏牙將潘晏、臧延範等，逐出節度使羅周翰。）〉
units.en: (The 《Ouyang History》 says Shihou killed Pan Yan, Zang Yanfan, and other Wei staff officers and expelled commissioner Luo Zhouhan.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Ouyang History》 says: Shihou seized the chance to kill the Wei yamen generals Pan Yan, Zang Yanfan, and others and drove out military commissioner Luo Zhouhan.)〉

units.zh: 越二日，又有指揮使趙賓夜率部軍擐甲，俟旦為亂。
units.en: Two days later commander Zhao Bin armed his men by night to rise at dawn.
units.literal: Two days later another commander Zhao Bin by night led his unit in armor, waiting at dawn to make trouble.

units.zh: 師厚以衙兵圍捕，賓不能起，乃越城而遁；
units.en: Shihou's guards surrounded them; Bin could not break out and fled over the wall;
units.literal: Shihou with yamen troops surrounded and seized them; Bin could not rise and fled over the wall;

units.zh: 師厚遣騎追至肥鄉，擒其黨百餘人，歸斬於府門。
units.en: Cavalry ran him down at Feixiang, took a hundred-odd accomplices, and executed them before the yamen.
units.literal: Shihou sent cavalry in pursuit to Feixiang, captured more than a hundred of his party, and beheaded them at the prefectural gate.

units.zh: 友珪即以師厚為魏博節度使、檢校侍中。
units.en: Yougui appointed Shihou commissioner of Weibo and acting Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Yougui then made Shihou military commissioner of Weibo and acting Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 未幾，鎮人、晉人侵魏之北鄙，師厚率軍至唐店，破之，斬首五千級，擒其都將三十餘人。
units.en: Soon locals and Jin struck Wei's north; Shihou met them at Tangdian, killed five thousand, and took thirty-odd officers.
units.literal: Before long men of the circuit and Jin raiders struck Wei's northern border; Shihou led troops to Tangdian, broke them, beheaded five thousand, and captured more than thirty of their commanders.

units.zh: 是時師厚握河朔兵，威望振主，友珪患之，詔師厚赴闕。
units.en: Shihou now commanded Hebei and towered over the throne; Yougui, uneasy, summoned him to court.
units.literal: At that time Shihou held the Hebei armies and his prestige shook the ruler; Yougui feared him and ordered Shihou to come to court.

units.zh: 師厚乃率精甲萬人至洛陽，嚴兵於都外，自以十餘人入謁，友珪懼，厚禮而遣之。
units.en: He marched ten thousand elite to Luoyang, camped in force outside the walls, and entered with only a dozen followers; Yougui feared him, honored him lavishly, and let him go.
units.literal: Shihou then led ten thousand picked men to Luoyang, drew up in strength outside the capital, and entered audience with only a dozen-odd men; Yougui was afraid, treated him with great courtesy, and sent him away.

units.zh: 及末帝將圖友珪，遣使謀於師厚，深陳款效，且馳書於侍衛軍使袁象先及主軍大將；
units.en: When the Last Emperor moved against Yougui he won Shihou's pledge and wrote urgently to guard commissioner Yuan Xiangxian and the chief commanders;
units.literal: When the Last Emperor was about to plot against Yougui he sent envoys to consult Shihou, who pledged deep loyalty and also rushed letters to the palace guard commissioner Yuan Xiangxian and the chief generals;

units.zh: 又遣都指揮使朱漢賓率兵至滑州以應禁旅。
units.en: and sent overall commander Zhu Hanbin to Hua to back the palace troops.
units.literal: he also sent overall commander Zhu Hanbin with troops to Hua to support the palace guard.

units.zh: 友珪既誅，末帝即位於東京，首封師厚為鄴王，加檢校太師、中書令。
units.en: When Yougui fell the Last Emperor enthroned himself at the Eastern Capital and first made Shihou Prince of Ye, Grand Preceptor, and Chief Minister.
units.literal: After Yougui was executed the Last Emperor took the throne at the Eastern Capital and first enfeoffed Shihou as Prince of Ye, advancing him to acting Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister.

units.zh: 每下詔不名，以官呼之，事無巨細，必先謀於師厚，師厚頗亦驕誕。
units.en: Edicts no longer named him but called him by title; every matter, great or small, went first to Shihou, and he grew arrogant.
units.literal: In every edict his name was not written—he was called by office—and whether the matter was great or small it was first discussed with Shihou; Shihou in turn grew quite proud and insolent.

units.zh: 先是，鎮人以我柏鄉不利之後，屢擾邊境，師厚總大軍直抵鎮州城下，焚蕩閭舍，移軍掠槁城、束鹿，至深州而歸。
units.en: Earlier, after our setback at Baixiang the men of Zhen had repeatedly raided the border; Shihou led the main army straight to Zhenzhou below the walls, burned and swept hamlets, shifted the army to plunder Gaocheng and Shulu, and returned from Shenzhou.
units.literal: Earlier, after our setback at Baixiang the men of Zhen had repeatedly raided the border; Shihou led the main army straight to Zhenzhou below the walls, burned and swept hamlets, shifted the army to plunder Gaocheng and Shulu, and returned from Shenzhou.

units.zh: 乾化五年三月，卒於鎮。
units.en: In the third month of Qianhua 5 he died at his post.
units.literal: Qianhua year 5, third month, he died in his post.

units.zh: 廢朝三日，贈太師。
units.en: Mourning halted court for three days; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Court mourning was suspended three days; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 師厚純謹敏幹，深為太祖知遇，委以重兵劇鎮，他莫能及。
units.en: Pure, careful, and capable, Shihou won the Founder's deepest trust and held the heaviest commands as no one else did.
units.literal: Shihou was pure, careful, and quick in affairs; the Founder knew and favored him deeply, entrusting him with heavy armies and hard circuits as no other could match.

units.zh: 然而末年矜功恃眾，驟萌不軌之意，於是專割財賦，置銀槍效節軍凡數千人，皆選摘驍銳，縱恣豢養，復故時牙軍之態，時人病之。
units.en: In old age he swaggered over his troops, skimmed the treasury, raised several thousand Silver Spear guards picked for brutality, pampered them, and brought back the old yamen-army arrogance that the people hated.
units.literal: Yet in his last years he prided himself on merit and relied on his masses; suddenly he harbored disloyal intent; he then monopolized revenues and levies, established a Silver Spear and Effected Discipline army of several thousand men, all picked for fierceness, indulged and fed at will, and revived the old yamen-army ways—men resented it.

units.zh: 向時河朔之俗，上元比屋夜遊，及師厚作鎮，乃課魏人戶立燈竿，千釭萬炬，洞照一城，縱士女嬉遊。
units.en: Hebei families once roamed all night at Lantern Festival; Shihou forced every Wei household to raise lamp poles until thousands of lights blazed over the city and soldiers and women caroused in the streets.
units.literal: Formerly in Hebei on the Lantern Festival every household roamed by night; when Shihou governed he levied on Wei households to set lamp poles—thousands of lamps, tens of thousands of torches—lighting the whole city, and let soldiers and women roam in sport.

units.zh: 復彩畫舟舫，令女妓棹歌於御河，縱酒彌日。
units.en: He painted pleasure boats, set courtesans to pole and sing on the imperial canal, and feasted for days on end.
units.literal: He also painted pleasure boats and had singing girls pole and sing on the imperial canal, drinking wine for whole days.

units.zh: 又於黎陽采巨石，將紀德政，以鐵車負載，驅牛數百以拽之，所至之處，丘墓廬舍悉皆毀壞，百姓望之，皆曰「碑來」。
units.en: At Liyang he took a great stone for a virtue monument, loaded it on an iron cart, and drove hundreds of oxen to drag it; graves and homes in its path were smashed, and people cried, "The stele is coming."
units.literal: Again at Liyang he quarried a huge stone to record his virtuous rule; an iron cart bore it, and several hundred oxen were driven to haul it; wherever it passed, mounds, tombs, and houses were all destroyed; the people on seeing it all said "The stele is coming."

units.zh: 及碑石才至，而師厚卒，魏人以為「悲來」之應。
units.en: The stone had barely arrived when Shihou died; Wei folk heard in "The stele is coming" the omen "Grief is coming."
units.literal: When the stone had only just arrived Shihou died; the people of Wei took it as the omen of "grief is coming."

units.zh: 末帝聞其卒也，於私庭受賀，乃議裂魏州為兩鎮。
units.en: The Last Emperor rejoiced privately at the news and planned to split Wei in two.
units.literal: The Last Emperor, hearing of his death, rejoiced in private and then debated splitting Wei into two circuits.

units.zh: 既而所樹親軍，果為叛亂，以招外寇，致使河朔淪陷，宗社覆滅，由師厚兆之也。
units.en: Soon his private guard rebelled, called in foreign enemies, and Hebei fell with the dynasty—the trail began with Shihou.
units.literal: Before long the personal army he had raised indeed rebelled, inviting outside raiders, until Hebei was lost and the altars overturned—the beginning lay with Shihou.

units.zh: 牛存節，字讚貞，青州博昌人也。
units.en: Niu Cunjie, who styled himself Zanzhen, came from Bochang in Qingzhou.
units.literal: Niu Cunjie, styled Zanzhen, was a man of Bochang in Qingzhou.

units.zh: 本名禮，太祖改而字之。
units.en: His original name was Li; the Founder changed it and gave him his courtesy name.
units.literal: His original name was Li; the Founder changed it and gave him this style.

units.zh: 少以雄勇自負。
units.en: As a youth he counted on his strength and daring.
units.literal: In youth he prided himself on fierce courage.

units.zh: 唐乾符末，鄉人諸葛爽為河陽節度使，存節往從之。
units.en: Late in Qianfu his fellow townsman Zhuge Shuang took Heyang; Cunjie entered his service.
units.literal: Late Tang Qianfu, his townsman Zhuge Shuang became military commissioner of Heyang; Cunjie went to follow him.

units.zh: 爽卒，存節謂同輩曰：「天下洶洶，當擇英主事之，以圖富貴。」
units.en: After Shuang's death Cunjie told his fellows, "The empire boils; choose a great master, serve him, and win rank and riches."
units.literal: When Shuang died, Cunjie told his comrades: "The realm is in turmoil; one should choose an outstanding lord to serve and seek wealth and honor."

units.zh: 遂歸於太祖。
units.en: Then he joined the Founder.
units.literal: Thereupon he went over to the Founder.

units.zh: 初授宣義軍小將。
units.en: He began as a junior officer in the Xuanyi army.
units.literal: At first he was appointed a minor officer of the Xuanyi army.

units.zh: 屬蔡寇至金堤驛，犯酸棗、靈昌，存節日與之鬥，凡二十餘往，每往必執俘而還，前後斬首二十餘級，獲孳畜甚眾。
units.en: When Cai rebels hit Jindi and raided Suanzao and Lingchang, he fought them twenty-odd times in as many days, always bringing back prisoners, twenty heads, and great herds of booty.
units.literal: When Cai bandits reached Jindi post, violating Suanzao and Lingchang, Cunjie fought them daily for more than twenty rounds; each time he returned with captives; in all he beheaded more than twenty and seized very many livestock.

units.zh: 太祖擊蔡賊於板橋、赤岡、酸棗門、封禪寺、枯河北，存節皆預其行，與諸將於濮州南劉橋、範縣大破鄆眾，自此深為太祖獎遇。
units.en: He fought with the Founder at Banqiao, Chigang, Suanzao Gate, Fengchan Temple, and north of the dry river, and with the other generals routed Yan troops at Liuqiao south of Pu and in Fan—after which the Founder prized him highly.
units.literal: The Founder struck Cai bandits at Banqiao, Chigang, Suanzao Gate, Fengchan Temple, and north of the withered river; Cunjie took part in every march; with the generals he broke Yan forces south of Pu at Liuqiao and in Fan county, and from then on won the Founder's deep favor.

units.zh: 文德元年夏，李罕之以並軍圍張宗奭於河陽，太祖遣存節率軍赴之。
units.en: In the summer of Wende 1 Li Hanzhi besieged Zhang Zongshuang at Heyang with Bing troops; the Founder sent Cunjie to relieve him.
units.literal: Wende year 1, summer, Li Hanzhi with Bing troops besieged Zhang Zongshuang at Heyang; the Founder sent Cunjie with troops to relieve him.

units.zh: 屬歲歉，餉饋不至，村民有儲幹椹者，存節以器用、錢帛易之，以給軍食。
units.en: Famine blocked supplies; Cunjie bought dried mulberry the villagers had stored, paying with goods and cash to feed his men.
units.literal: It was a lean year and rations did not arrive; villagers had stored dry mulberry; Cunjie traded vessels and silks for it to feed the army.

units.zh: 大破賊於浿河，罕之引眾北走。
units.en: He crushed the enemy on the Pei; Hanzhi fled north.
units.literal: He greatly defeated the bandits on the Pei River; Hanzhi led his host north in flight.

units.zh: 又預討徐、宿有功。
units.en: He later fought at Xu and Su with distinction.
units.literal: He also took part in the campaigns against Xu and Su with merit.

units.zh: 及討河北，存節前鋒下黎陽，收臨河，至內黃西，以兵千餘人當魏人萬二千眾，大破其陣，僵仆蔽野。
units.en: On the Hebei campaign he took Liyang and Linhe in the van; west of Neihuang a thousand men routed twelve thousand Wei troops until the field was heaped with corpses.
units.literal: In the Hebei campaign Cunjie as vanguard took Liyang and Linhe; west of Neihuang with a little more than a thousand men he met twelve thousand Wei troops and broke their line; the dead covered the field.

units.zh: 太祖深所歎激，謂有神兵之助。
units.en: The Founder marveled and said heaven had sent him soldiers.
units.literal: The Founder sighed in deep admiration and said divine soldiers had aided him.

units.zh: 大順元年，改滑州左右廂牢城使。
units.en: In Dashun 1 he became commander of both wings of Hua's garrison force.
units.literal: Dashun year 1, he was changed to commander of the left and right wings of Hua's garrison.

units.zh: 與諸將討時溥，累破賊軍。
units.en: He joined the generals against Shi Pu and broke his armies again and again.
units.literal: With the generals he campaigned against Shi Pu and repeatedly broke his armies.

units.zh: 景福元年秋，改遏後都指揮使。
units.en: In the autumn of Jingfu 1 he was made commander of the Rearward Check.
units.literal: Jingfu year 1, autumn, he was changed to commander of the Rearward Check.

units.zh: 攻濮之役，領軍先登，遂拔其壘。
units.en: At Pu he led the first escalade and took the camp.
units.literal: In the attack on Pu he led the army in the first ascent and then stormed the stockade.

units.zh: 二年四月，下徐州，梟時溥，存節力戰，其功居多。
units.en: In the fourth month of year 2 Xuzhou fell and Shi Pu's head was sent up; Cunjie's fighting won the largest share of credit.
units.literal: Year 2, fourth month, Xuzhou fell; Shi Pu was displayed; Cunjie fought hard and his merit was greatest.

units.zh: 乾寧二年，授檢校工部尚書。
units.en: In Qianning 2 he was made acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: Qianning year 2, he was appointed acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 三年夏，太祖東討鄆州，存節領軍次故樂亭，扼其要路，都指揮使龐師古屯馬頰，存節密與都將王言謀入鄆壘。
units.en: In the summer of year 3 the Founder marched on Yan; Cunjie blocked the road at old Leting while Pang Shigu camped at Majia; Cunjie and commander Wang Yan plotted a night entry into Yan.
units.literal: Year 3, summer, the Founder campaigned east against Yan; Cunjie led troops to halt at old Leting, blocking the vital road; overall commander Pang Shigu camped at Majia; Cunjie secretly plotted with commander Wang Yan to enter the Yan ramparts.

units.zh: 十二月，存節遣王言夜伏勇士於州西北，以船逾濠，舉梯登陴。
units.en: In the twelfth month he sent Wang Yan to hide men northwest of the city; boats crossed the ditch and ladders reached the parapet.
units.literal: Twelfth month, Cunjie sent Wang Yan by night to hide brave men northwest of the prefecture; boats crossed the moat and ladders went up the wall.

units.zh: 既而王言不克入，存節獨率伏軍負梯童破其西甕城，奪其濠橋，諸軍俱進。
units.en: Wang Yan could not enter; Cunjie alone led the hidden troops bearing ladders in a mass assault on the west barbican, seized the moat bridge, and all armies advanced together.
units.literal: Wang Yan could not enter; Cunjie alone led the hidden troops bearing ladders in a mass assault on the west barbican, seized the moat bridge, and all armies advanced together.

units.zh: 四年四月，陷其城，尋與葛從周降下兗州，加檢校右僕射。
units.en: In the fourth month of year 4 the city fell; with Ge Congzhou he then took Yan and rose to acting Right Vice Director.
units.literal: Year 4, fourth month, the city fell; soon with Ge Congzhou he took Yanzhou and was advanced to acting Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 其年秋，大舉以伐淮南，至濠州東，聞前軍失利於清口，諸軍退至間河，無復隊伍。
units.en: That autumn the great Huainan expedition reached east of Hao, learned the vanguard had lost at Qingkou, and fell back to Jian River in disorder.
units.literal: That autumn a great campaign went against Huainan; reaching east of Hao they heard the vanguard had been defeated at Qingkou; the armies withdrew to Jian River and no longer kept formation.

units.zh: 存節遏其後，諸將釋騎步鬥，諸軍稍得濟，收合所部並敗兵共八千餘人，至於淮涘，時不食已四日矣。
units.en: Cunjie held the rear while generals fought on foot; units straggled across; he rallied his own men and stragglers—eight thousand—and reached the Huai starving after four days without food.
units.literal: Cunjie brought up the rear; the generals dismounted to fight on foot; the armies little by little crossed; he gathered his own command and the defeated troops together, more than eight thousand men; reaching the Huai bank they had not eaten for four days.

units.zh: 存節訓勵部分，以禦追寇，遂得旋師。
units.en: He drilled and formed them against pursuit and brought the column home.
units.literal: Cunjie encouraged and arrayed them to meet pursuing raiders and was able to turn the army about.

units.zh: 五年，除亳州刺史，俄遷宣武軍都指揮使，改宿州刺史。
units.en: In year 5 he became prefect of Bo, soon Xuanwu commander, then governor of Su.
units.literal: Year 5, he was made prefect of Bo; soon he was advanced to overall commander of the Xuanwu army and changed to prefect of Su.

units.zh: 明年，淮賊大至彭城，存節乃以部下兵夜發，直趣彭門；
units.en: Next year Huai rebels swarmed Pengcheng; Cunjie marched by night straight for the Peng gate;
units.literal: The next year Huai bandits came in force to Pengcheng; Cunjie then set out by night with his command and went straight to the Peng gate;

units.zh: 淮人訝其神速，震恐而退，諸將服其智識。
units.en: the Huai were stunned by his speed and fled; the other generals praised his judgment.
units.literal: the Huai men marveled at his speed, were shaken and withdrew, and the generals admired his resource.

units.zh: 光化二年，罷歸，復為左衙都將兼馬步教練使。
units.en: In Guanghua 2 he was dismissed to return home, then reappointed commander of the Left Garrison and joint horse-and-foot drill instructor.
units.literal: Guanghua year 2, dismissed and returned, again made commander of the Left Garrison and also horse-and-foot drill instructor.

units.zh: 天復元年，授潞州馬步都指揮使，法令嚴整，士庶安之。
units.en: In Tianfu 1 he was made Lu's horse-and-foot commander; his regulations were strict and the people lived secure.
units.literal: Tianfu year 1, appointed overall horse-and-foot commander of Lu; laws and orders were strict and orderly, officials and people were at peace.

units.zh: 及追赴行在，士卒泣送者不絕於道，加金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空，改滑州左衙步軍指揮使，知邢州軍州事。
units.en: Summoned to court, troops wept along the road as he left; he rose to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Cassia seal and acting Minister of Works, became commander of Hua Left Garrison infantry, and acted as Xing prefect and military commissioner.
units.literal: When summoned to the imperial camp, soldiers weeping to see him off lined the road without end; he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with the Golden Cassia seal and acting Minister of Works, changed to commander of Hua's Left Garrison foot army, and made acting military commissioner of Xing.

units.zh: 天祐元年，授邢州團練使。
units.en: In Tianyou 1 he received Xing as defense commissioner.
units.literal: Tianyou year 1, appointed defense commissioner of Xing.

units.zh: 時州兵才及二百人，晉人知之，以大軍來寇。
units.en: The prefecture had only two hundred troops; the Jin learned this and marched in force.
units.literal: At the time the prefectural troops numbered barely two hundred; the Jin learned of it and came raiding with a great army.

units.zh: 太祖在鄴，發長直兵二千人赴援，存節率壯健出鬥，以家財賞激戰士，並軍急攻，七日不能克而去。
units.en: At Ye the Founder sent two thousand long-service men; Cunjie led his best troops out, paid warriors from his own purse, and with the relief force assaulted hard for seven days before the enemy withdrew.
units.literal: The Founder was at Ye and sent two thousand long-service troops to the relief; Cunjie led the strong men out to fight, rewarded the warriors with his household wealth to spur them on; the allied armies pressed the attack fiercely but after seven days could not take the place and withdrew.

units.zh: 太祖召至，勞慰久之，厚賚金帛鞍馬，加檢校司徒。
units.en: The Founder summoned him, consoled him at length, gave rich gifts of gold, silk, saddles and horses, and made him acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: The Founder summoned him, comforted him at length, richly rewarded him with gold, silks, saddles, and horses, and advanced him to acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 冬，罷軍，署為元帥府左都押衙。
units.en: That winter the army was stood down and he was made Left Chief Escort of the Marshal's headquarters.
units.literal: Winter, the army was disbanded; he was appointed Left Chief Escort Officer of the Marshal's headquarters.

units.zh: 四年，太祖受禪，除右千牛衛上將軍。
units.en: In year 4, when the Founder took the throne, he was made senior general of the Right Palace Guard.
units.literal: Year 4, when the Founder received the abdication, he was appointed senior general of the Right Palace Guard.

units.zh: 其秋，攻潞州，以存節為行營馬步軍都排陣使。
units.en: That autumn, during the Lu campaign, he was named the field army's master of battle arrays for horse and foot.
units.literal: That autumn, attacking Lu Prefecture, Cunjie was made overall array-master of the camp horse and foot.

units.zh: 開平二年二月，自右監門衛上將軍轉右龍虎統軍，駐留洛下。
units.en: In the second month of Kaiping 2 he rose from Right Gate Guard senior general to commander of the Right Dragon-Tiger army and stayed at Luoyang.
units.literal: Kaiping year 2, second month, from Right Gate Guard senior general he was changed to Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief, remaining at Luoyang.

units.zh: 是歲，王師敗於上黨，晉人乘勝進迫澤州，州城將陷。
units.en: That year Wang's force lost at Shangdang; the Jin swept on toward Ze, and the city was near collapse.
units.literal: That year Wang's army was defeated at Shangdang; Jin men pressed the victory and advanced on Zezhou; the city was about to fall.

units.zh: 河南留守張全義召存節謀，遂以本軍及右龍虎、羽林等軍往應接上黨。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi, regent of Henan, called Cunjie; he marched his own troops plus the Right Dragon-Tiger and Feathered Forest to relieve Shangdang.
units.literal: Henan regent Zhang Quanyi summoned Cunjie to counsel; he then led his own army and the Right Dragon-Tiger, Feathered Forest, and other armies to answer Shangdang.

units.zh: 師至天並關，存節謂諸將曰：「是行也，雖不奉詔旨，然要害之地，不可致失。」
units.en: At Tianbing Pass Cunjie told his officers, "We have no fresh orders, but this choke point cannot be abandoned."
units.literal: When the army reached Tianbing Pass, Cunjie told the generals: "On this march, though we do not carry imperial orders, yet this vital place must not be lost."

units.zh: 時晉人新勝，其鋒甚盛，存節引從而前，銜枚夜至澤州，適遇守埤者已縱火鼓噪，以應外軍，刺史保衙城，不知所為。
units.en: The Jin were fresh from victory and fierce; Cunjie pushed on, marched by night with gags, and reached Ze as the wall guards were already firing beacons and shouting to the relief force; the prefect held the yamen city and did not know what to do.
units.literal: At that time the Jin had just won and their edge was very sharp; Cunjie led his followers forward, marched at night with gags in the men's mouths, and reached Ze; he happened on the wall guards already lighting fires and shouting to answer the outside army; the prefect held the yamen city and did not know what to do.

units.zh: 存節才入，晉軍已至矣，乃分布守禦。
units.en: He had barely entered when the Jin arrived; he spread his men for defense.
units.literal: Cunjie had only just entered when Jin troops were already there; he then deployed for defense.

units.zh: 晉軍四面攻鬥，開地道以入城，存節亦以隧道應之，逆戰於地中，晉軍不能進；
units.en: The Jin assaulted from four sides and mined under the wall; Cunjie mined back and met them underground until they could not advance;
units.literal: Jin troops attacked on four sides, opened tunnels into the city; Cunjie also met them with tunnels and fought them underground; the Jin could not advance;

units.zh: 又以勁弩射之，中者人馬皆洞，經十三日，晉軍死傷者甚眾，焚營而退，郡以獲全，太祖屢歎賞之。
units.en: he raked them with heavy crossbows that pierced men and horses; after thirteen days the Jin losses were heavy; they burned their camp and left; the prefecture was saved, and the Founder praised him again and again.
units.literal: he also shot them with powerful crossbows; those hit, man and horse alike, were pierced through; after thirteen days Jin dead and wounded were very many; they burned camp and withdrew; the commandery was preserved whole; the Founder repeatedly sighed in praise.

units.zh: 五月，遷左龍虎統軍，充六軍馬步都指揮使。
units.en: In the fifth month he became commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger army and supreme horse-and-foot commander of the Six Armies.
units.literal: Fifth month, he was moved to Left Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and filled the post of overall horse-and-foot commander of the Six Armies.

units.zh: 十月，授絳州刺史。
units.en: In the tenth month he was made prefect of Jiang.
units.literal: Tenth month, he was appointed Jiang prefect.

units.zh: 三年四月，除鄜州留後。
units.en: In the fourth month of year 3 he was appointed regent of Fuzhou.
units.literal: Year 3, fourth month, appointed Fuzhou regent.

units.zh: 六月，劉知俊以同州叛，尋授同州留後，未幾，加檢校太保、同州節度使。
units.en: In the sixth month Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; Cunjie was soon made regent there, then honorary Grand Guardian and military commissioner of Tong.
units.literal: June, Liu Zhijun rebelled at Tongzhou; soon he was appointed Tongzhou regent; before long, added honorary Grand Guardian and Tongzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 乾化二年，加檢校太傅，進封開國公。
units.en: In Qianhua 2 he was made honorary Grand Mentor and advanced to Founding Duke.
units.literal: Qianhua year 2, added honorary Grand Mentor, advanced to Founding Duke.

units.zh: 存節戒嚴軍旅，常若敵至。
units.en: Cunjie kept his troops on war footing as though the enemy were always near.
units.literal: Cunjie kept the army on strict alert as if the enemy were always at hand.

units.zh: 先是，州中井水鹹苦，人不可飲。
units.en: The city wells had long been brackish and undrinkable.
units.literal: Earlier, the prefectural wells were brackish and bitter, unfit to drink.

units.zh: 及並人、岐人來迫州城，或以為兵士渴乏，陷在旦夕。
units.en: When Jin and Qi armies besieged the city, some feared the troops would die of thirst and the walls would fall within days.
units.literal: When Bing and Qi men came to press the city, some thought the soldiers would die of thirst and the city would fall within days.

units.zh: 存節及肅拜虔祝，擇地鑿八十餘井，其味皆甘淡，由是人馬汲濯有餘，眾以為至誠之感。
units.en: Cunjie bowed and prayed, then sank more than eighty wells whose water was sweet and clear; men and horses had plenty to drink, and the people called it a reward for his sincerity.
units.literal: Cunjie solemnly bowed and prayed devoutly, chose ground and sank more than eighty wells; all tasted sweet and mild; thus men and horses had water to draw and wash in abundance; the mass took it as a response to utmost sincerity.

units.zh: 自八月至三年春末，人馬未嘗釋甲，以至寇退。
units.en: From the eighth month through the spring of year 3 his men never doffed armor until the enemy withdrew.
units.literal: From the eighth month to the end of spring in year 3, men and horses never removed armor, until the raiders withdrew.

units.zh: 尋加同平章事，詔赴闕。
units.en: He was soon made Tongping Grand Councilor and summoned to court.
units.literal: Soon added Tongping Grand Councilor; an edict ordered him to the capital.

units.zh: 末帝召慰勉，賞賜甚厚。
units.en: The Last Emperor received him with warm praise and rich gifts.
units.literal: The Last Emperor summoned him to comfort and encourage him; rewards were very generous.

units.zh: 十一月，加開府儀同三司，食邑一千戶，授鄆州節度使。
units.en: In the eleventh month he was given permission to open an office with honors equal to the Three Dukes, a thousand-household fief, and the Yanzhou command.
units.literal: Eleventh month, added Permitted to Open an Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes, food domain one thousand households, appointed Yanzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 四年，加淮南西北面行營招討使，控扼淮濆，邊境安之。
units.en: In year 4 he was made pacification commissioner for the northwest Huainan campaign, held the Huai shore, and kept the frontier quiet.
units.literal: Year 4, added northwest Huainan campaign line-army pacification commissioner, controlled the Huai embankment region; the border was secure.

units.zh: 其冬，蔣殷據徐州逆命，存節方以大眾戍潁州，得殷逆謀，密以上聞，遽奉詔與劉鄩同討之，頓於埇上。
units.en: That winter Jiang Yin rebelled at Xuzhou while Cunjie was at Yingzhou with a large force; he reported in secret, received orders to join Liu Zhen, and encamped at Yong.
units.literal: That winter, Jiang Yin held Xuzhou in defiance of orders; Cunjie was then garrisoning Yingzhou with a large host; learning of Yin's rebellion, he secretly reported above; hastily received an edict with Liu Zhen jointly to suppress him; encamped at Yong.

units.zh: 淮賊朱瑾以兵救殷，距宿之兩舍，聞存節兵大至，即委糧棄甲而遁，竟平徐州。
units.en: Zhu Jin of Huai marched to relieve Yin, but two stages from Su he heard Cunjie was coming in force, abandoned stores and arms, and fled; Xuzhou was pacified.
units.literal: Huai rebel Zhu Jin led troops to rescue Yin; at two stages from Su he heard Cunjie's army was great and coming; he abandoned grain and armor and fled; Xuzhou was pacified in the end.

units.zh: 詔加太尉。
units.en: An edict made him Grand Marshal.
units.literal: An edict added Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 夏中病渴且痟，屬河北用軍，末帝令率軍屯陽留以張劉鄩之勢。
units.en: Midsummer he fell ill with fever and malaria; with Hebei in crisis the Last Emperor sent him to Yangliu to stiffen Liu Zhen's line.
units.literal: Midsummer he suffered wasting thirst and malaria; as Hebei was in campaign, the Last Emperor ordered him to lead the army to encamp at Yangliu to strengthen Liu Zhen's position.

units.zh: 存節忠憤彌篤，未嘗言病，料敵治戎，旦夕愈厲。
units.en: His loyal zeal only sharpened; he never mentioned his illness and grew sterner each day in reading the enemy and commanding the host.
units.literal: Cunjie's loyal indignation grew ever fiercer; he never spoke of illness; estimating the enemy and governing the host, morning and night grew the sterner.

units.zh: 病革，詔歸汶陽，翌日而卒。
units.en: When he worsened, an edict recalled him to Wenyang; he died the next day.
units.literal: When illness turned critical, an edict sent him back to Wenyang; the next day he died.

units.zh: 將終，戒其子知業、知讓等以忠孝，言不及他。
units.en: Dying, he urged his sons Zhiye and Zhirang to loyalty and filial piety and said nothing else.
units.literal: On the verge of death he admonished his sons Zhiye, Zhirang and others with loyalty and filial piety, speaking of nothing else.

units.zh: 冊贈太師。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 存節武鷙慷慨，有大節，野戰壁守，皆其所長，威名聞於境外，深為末帝所重，而木強忠厚，有賈復之風焉。
units.en: Fierce, generous, and resolute, he excelled in the field and behind walls; his fame reached beyond the border and the Last Emperor prized him, yet he was bluntly honest in the manner of Jia Fu.
units.literal: Cunjie was martially fierce and generously spirited, with great integrity; field battle and wall defense were alike his strengths; his martial fame was heard beyond the borders; the Last Emperor valued him deeply, yet he was stubbornly honest and loyal, having the manner of Jia Fu.

units.zh: 王檀，字眾美，京兆人也。
units.en: Wang Tan, styled Zhongmei, came from Jingzhao.
units.literal: Wang Tan, style Zhongmei, was a native of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 曾祖泚，唐左金吾衛將軍、隴州防禦使。
units.en: His great-grandfather Chi had been Left Golden Guard general and defense commissioner of Long.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Chi was Left Golden Guard general of Tang and Longzhou defense commissioner.

units.zh: 祖曜，定難功臣、渭橋鎮遏使。
units.en: His grandfather Yao was a Pacifier of Difficulties merit lord and commissioner at Wei Bridge.
units.literal: His grandfather Yao was a Pacifier of Difficulties merit lord and Wei Bridge suppression commissioner.

units.zh: 父環，鴻臚卿，以檀貴，累贈左僕射。
units.en: His father Huan was Chamberlain for Dependencies and, through Tan's eminence, was repeatedly granted posthumous promotion to Left Vice Director.
units.literal: His father Huan was Chamberlain for Dependencies; because Tan was honored, he was repeatedly granted posthumous advancement to Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 檀少英悟，美形儀，好讀兵書，洞曉韜略。
units.en: As a youth Tan was quick-witted and handsome, read military works, and mastered strategy.
units.literal: Tan in youth was keen and clever, handsome in bearing, loved reading military books, and thoroughly understood strategy.

units.zh: 唐中和中，太祖鎮大梁，檀為小將。
units.en: In Tang Zhonghe, when the Founder held Daliang, Tan served as a junior officer.
units.literal: In Zhonghe of Tang the Founder held Daliang; Tan was a junior officer.

units.zh: 四年，汴將楊彥洪破巢將尚讓、李讜於尉氏門外，檀在戰中，摧鋒陷陣，遂為太祖所知，稍蒙擢用。
units.en: In year 4 Yang Yanhong of Bian defeated Shang Rang and Li Dang outside Weishi Gate; Tan fought in the van, broke the enemy line, won the Founder's notice, and rose in rank.
units.literal: Year 4, Bian general Yang Yanhong defeated Chao generals Shang Rang and Li Dang outside the Weishi Gate; Tan was in the battle, shattered the van and broke the array, and thus came to the Founder's notice and gradually received promotion.

units.zh: 預破蔡賊於斤溝、淝河、八角，遷踏白都副將。
units.en: He helped defeat Cai rebels at Jingou, the Fei, and Bajiao and became deputy commander of the Taibai corps.
units.literal: He took part in defeating Cai bandits at Jingou, Fei River, and Bajiao, and was moved to deputy commander of the Taibai corps.

units.zh: 光啟二年，從胡真擊淮西之眾，解河陽之圍。
units.en: In Guangqi 2 he followed Hu Zhen against Huaixi and raised the siege of Heyang.
units.literal: Guangqi year 2, he followed Hu Zhen to strike Huaixi forces and lifted the siege of Heyang.

units.zh: 蔡賊張存敢乘亂據洛陽，檀與勇士數十人潛入賊柵，邀其輜重，存敢遁走。
units.en: Zhang Cungan of Cai seized Luoyang in the turmoil; Tan slipped into the camp with a few dozen men, seized their baggage, and Cungan fled.
units.literal: Cai bandit Zhang Cungan took advantage of disorder to hold Luoyang; Tan with several dozen brave men secretly entered the bandit camp, intercepted their baggage train, and Cungan fled.

units.zh: 胡真至陝州，開通貢路，遣檀攻玉山寨，降賊帥石令殷。
units.en: At Shaanzhou Hu Zhen opened the tribute route and sent Tan against Yushan stockade, where he subdued the bandit chief Shi Lingyin.
units.literal: When Hu Zhen reached Shaanzhou and opened the tribute road, he sent Tan to attack Yushan stockade and reduce bandit chief Shi Lingyin.

units.zh: 從擊秦宗賢於鄭州西北河灘之上，於太祖馬前射賊將孫安，應弦而斃。
units.en: At the river beach northwest of Zhengzhou he shot the bandit general Sun An dead before the Founder's horse.
units.literal: Joining the attack on Qin Zongxian on the river beach northwest of Zhengzhou, before the Founder's horse he shot bandit general Sun An, who fell at the twang of the bowstring.

units.zh: 三年，佐都指揮使朱珍敗徐戎於孫師陂，獲其將孫用和、束詡以獻。
units.en: In year 3, aiding Zhu Zhen, he defeated Xu forces at Sunshi Slope and presented the generals Sun Yonghe and Shu Xu.
units.literal: Year 3, assisting overall commander Zhu Zhen he defeated Xu troops at Sunshi Slope and presented their generals Sun Yonghe and Shu Xu.

units.zh: 從擊蔡賊於板橋，偏將李重裔追賊馬躓，為蔡人所擒，檀奪取而旋，獲賊將薛注。
units.en: At Banqiao, when Li Chongyi's horse fell and Cai men seized him, Tan rescued him and captured the bandit general Xue Zhu.
units.literal: Joining the attack on Cai bandits at Banqiao, deputy general Li Chongyi in pursuit had his horse stumble and was seized by Cai men; Tan snatched him back and captured bandit general Xue Zhu.

units.zh: 太祖破朱瑾於劉橋，檀盡收其軍實。
units.en: When the Founder beat Zhu Jin at Liuchiao, Tan gathered all his supplies.
units.literal: When the Founder defeated Zhu Jin at Liuchiao, Tan gathered all his military stores.

units.zh: 文德元年三月，討羅宏信，敗魏人於內黃，檀獲其將周儒、邵神劍以歸，補衝山都虞候。
units.en: In the third month of Wende 1, campaigning against Luo Hongxin, he defeated Wei troops at Neihuang, took Zhou Ru and Shao Shenjian, and was made commandant of the Chongshan corps.
units.literal: Wende era year 1, third month, campaigning against Luo Hongxin he defeated Wei men at Neihuang; Tan captured their generals Zhou Ru and Shao Shenjian and returned, and was made commandant of the Chongshan corps.

units.zh: 是歲，與諸軍平蔡州。
units.en: That year he joined in the pacification of Caizhou.
units.literal: That year he joined the armies in pacifying Caizhou.

units.zh: 明年，佐朱珍大破時溥之眾，檀獲賊將何肱，改左踏白馬軍副將。
units.en: The next year, aiding Zhu Zhen, he routed Shi Pu and captured He Gong, then became deputy commander of the Left Taibai Horse Army.
units.literal: The next year, assisting Zhu Zhen he greatly defeated Shi Pu's host; Tan captured bandit general He Gong and was changed to deputy commander of the Left Taibai Horse Army.

units.zh: 預征兗、鄆，累立戰功。
units.en: He campaigned in Yan and Yun and won repeated distinction.
units.literal: He took part in the campaigns against Yan and Yun and repeatedly won battle merit.

units.zh: 大順元年，從龐師古渡淮深入，討孫儒之亂，奪邵伯堰，破高郵軍。
units.en: In Dashun 1 he followed Pang Shigu deep across the Huai against Sun Ru, took Shaobo weir, and routed the Gaoyou force.
units.literal: Dashun year 1, he followed Pang Shigu in crossing the Huai in depth to suppress Sun Ru's disorder, seized Shaobo weir, and broke the Gaoyou army.

units.zh: 檀奮命擊賊，刃傷左臂。
units.en: Tan fought desperately and took a blade wound in his left arm.
units.literal: Tan fought desperately against the bandits and was wounded in the left arm by a blade.

units.zh: 未幾，遷順義都將。
units.en: Soon he was made commander of Shunyi.
units.literal: Before long he was moved to commander of the Shunyi command.

units.zh: 天復中，從太祖率四鎮之師圍鳳翔，以迎昭宗。
units.en: In Tianfu he followed the Founder with the armies of four commands to besiege Fengxiang and restore Zhaozong.
units.literal: In Tianfu he followed the Founder leading the armies of four commands to besiege Fengxiang and welcome Zhaozong.

units.zh: 屢立戎效，遷左踏白指揮使。
units.en: He won repeated distinction and became commander of the Left Taibai corps.
units.literal: He repeatedly won military merit and was moved to commander of the Left Taibai corps.

units.zh: 從攻王師範於青州，檀以偏師收復密郡，
units.en: In the attack on Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Tan with a detached column recovered Mizhou,
units.literal: Joining the attack on Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Tan with a detached force recovered Mizhou,

units.zh: 〈（《永陽志》云：張訓守密州刺史，朱全忠至青州，訓謂諸將曰：「汴人將至，何以禦之？」
units.en: (The 《Record of Yongyang》 says Zhang Xun was prefect of Mizhou; when Zhu Quanzhong reached Qingzhou, Xun asked his officers, "The Bian army is coming—how shall we meet them?"
units.literal: (The 《Record of Yongyang》 says: Zhang Xun held the post of Mizhou prefect; Zhu Quanzhong reached Qingzhou; Xun said to the generals: "The men of Bian are coming—how shall we resist them?"

units.zh: 諸將請焚城大掠而歸。
units.en: His officers urged burning the city, looting it bare, and retreating.
units.literal: The generals asked to burn the city, plunder greatly, and return.

units.zh: 訓曰：「不可。」
units.en: Xun said, "That we cannot do."
units.literal: Xun said: "It cannot be done."

units.zh: 乃封府庫，植旗幟於城上，遣羸弱居前，自以精兵殿其後而去。
units.en: He sealed the treasury, raised banners on the walls, sent the weak forward, and withdrew with his best troops in the rear.
units.literal: Then he sealed the treasury, planted banners on the city walls, sent the weak ahead, and himself with crack troops brought up the rear and left.

units.zh: 全忠遣王檀攻密州，數日乃敢入城。）〉
units.en: Quanzhong sent Wang Tan against Mizhou, and only after several days did Tan dare enter the city.)〉
units.literal: Quanzhong sent Wang Tan to attack Mizhou; only after several days did he dare enter the city.)〉

units.zh: 遂權知軍州事，充本州馬步軍都指揮使，尋表授檢校右僕射，守密州刺史。
units.en: He then acted as military and civil commissioner of the prefecture and commander of its forces, and was soon made honorary Right Vice Director and defender of Mizhou.
units.literal: Thereupon he was made acting military and prefectural commissioner of the prefecture, commander of local horse and foot forces; soon memorialized as honorary Right Vice Director and defender of Mizhou prefect.

units.zh: 郡接淮戎，舊無壁壘，乃率夫修築羅城，六旬而畢，居民賴之，加檢校司空。
units.en: The prefecture bordered Huai rebels and had no walls; he built an outer rampart in sixty days, to the people's relief, and was made honorary Grand Master.
units.literal: The commandery bordered Huai bandits and formerly had no walls; he led laborers to build an outer wall, completing it in sixty days; the people relied on it; honorary Grand Master was added.

units.zh: 開平二年六月，授邢州保義軍節度使、檢校司徒。
units.en: In the sixth month of Kaiping 2 he was made Baoyi commissioner of Xing and honorary Minister of Works.
units.literal: Kaiping year 2, sixth month, appointed Baoyi army military commissioner of Xingzhou, honorary Minister of Works.

units.zh: 三年，加檢校太保，充潞州東北面行營招討使。
units.en: In year 3 he was made honorary Grand Guardian and pacification commissioner for the northeast Luzhou campaign.
units.literal: Year 3, added honorary Grand Guardian and made northeast Luzhou campaign line-army pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 乾化元年正月，王景仁與晉人戰於柏鄉，王師敗績，河朔大震。
units.en: In the first month of Qianhua 1, Wang Jingren fought the Jin at Baixiang; the imperial army was routed and Hebei was shaken.
units.literal: Qianhua year 1, first month, Wang Jingren fought Jin men at Baixiang; the royal army was badly defeated and Hebei was greatly shaken.

units.zh: 景仁與眾為敵騎所追，檀嚴設備，應接敗軍，助以資裝，獲濟者甚眾。
units.en: Jingren and his men were chased by enemy horse; Tan stood ready, received the fugitives, and supplied them so that many escaped.
units.literal: Jingren and the host were pursued by enemy cavalry; Tan made strict preparations and received the defeated army, aiding them with supplies; very many were able to cross over.

units.zh: 俄而晉軍大至，重圍四合，土山地穴，晝夜攻擊，太祖憂之。
units.en: Soon the Jin came in force, besieged the city on every side with ramparts and mines, and attacked day and night; the Founder was deeply worried.
units.literal: Before long the Jin army came in great force; on four sides they pressed close; earthworks and mining tunnels; day and night they attacked; the Founder was anxious.

units.zh: 檀密上表，請駕不親征，而悉力枝梧，竟全城壘。
units.en: Tan secretly urged the Founder not to take the field in person and braced the defense until the city held.
units.literal: Tan secretly memorialized, asking that the imperial carriage not go on campaign in person while he exerted all strength in support; in the end the whole city and ramparts were preserved.

units.zh: 三月，以功就加檢校太傅、同平章事。
units.en: In the third month his merit won him honorary Grand Mentor and Tongping Grand Councilor.
units.literal: Third month, for merit he was at once added honorary Grand Mentor and Tongping Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 七月，又加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，進封琅琊郡王，命宣徽使趙殷衡賚詔慰諭，賜絹千匹、銀千兩，賞守禦邢州之功也。
units.en: In the seventh month he was further granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Honored Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, and advancement to Prince of Langya; Zhao Yinheng brought the edict, with a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand taels of silver for holding Xing.
units.literal: Seventh month, again added Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Permitted to Open an Office with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes), honorary Grand Marshal, advanced to Prince of Langya commandery, ordered Palace Commissioner Zhao Yinheng to convey the edict in comfort, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand taels of silver—reward for defending Xingzhou.

units.zh: 庶人友珪僭位，授鄧州宣化軍節度使、檢校太尉、兼侍中。
units.en: When Yougui seized the throne he made Tan Xuanhua commissioner of Deng, honorary Grand Marshal, and concurrent Palace Attendant.
units.literal: The commoner Yougui usurped the throne and appointed him Xuanhua army military commissioner of Dengzhou, honorary Grand Marshal, and concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 末帝即位，移授許州匡國軍節度使，加檢校太師。
units.en: At the Last Emperor's accession he was moved to Kuangguo commissioner of Xu and made honorary Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he was transferred to Kuangguo army military commissioner of Xu and added honorary Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 五年，蔡州刺史王彥溫作亂，檀受詔討平之，加兼中書令。
units.en: In year 5, when Cai prefect Wang Yanwen rebelled, Tan was ordered to crush him and was made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: Year 5, Cai prefect Wang Yanwen rebelled; Tan received an edict to suppress and pacify him and was added concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 貞明元年三月，魏博軍亂。
units.en: In the third month of Zhenming 1 the Weibo army mutinied.
units.literal: Zhenming year 1, third month, the Weibo army mutinied.

units.zh: 六月，晉王入魏州，分兵收下屬郡，河北大擾，檀受詔與開封尹劉鄩犄角進師，以援河北。
units.en: In the sixth month the Prince of Jin took Weizhou and seized its dependencies; Hebei was in turmoil; Tan was ordered to advance with Liu Xun of Kaifeng in support of Hebei.
units.literal: Sixth month, the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou and sent troops in divisions to take subordinate commanderies; Hebei was greatly disturbed; Tan received an edict with Kaifeng Intendant Liu Xun to advance in pincer and aid Hebei.

units.zh: 檀攻澶州魏縣，下之，擒賊將李岩、王開關以獻。
units.en: Tan stormed Weixian in Chanzhou, captured it, and presented the rebel generals Li Yan and Wang Kaiguan.
units.literal: Tan attacked Weixian of Chuanzhou, took it, and presented bandit generals Li Yan and Wang Kaiguan.

units.zh: 頃之，檀密疏請以奇兵西趣河中，自陰地關襲取晉陽，末帝許之，即馳兵而去。
units.en: Soon he asked leave to strike west through Hezhong and take Jinyang by Yindi Pass; the Last Emperor agreed and he marched at once.
units.literal: Before long Tan secretly memorialized asking to take a picked force west to Hezhong and strike Jinyang by way of Yindi Pass; the Last Emperor approved; he at once galloped his troops away.

units.zh: 二年二月，師至晉陽，晝夜急攻其壘，并州幾陷。
units.en: In the second month of year 2 he reached Jinyang and assaulted its walls day and night until Bingzhou nearly fell.
units.literal: Year 2, second month, the army reached Jinyang; day and night they pressed the attack on its ramparts; Bingzhou nearly fell.

units.zh: 既而蕃將石家才自潞州以援兵至，檀引軍大掠而還。
units.en: When the foreign general Shi Jiacai marched from Luzhou with relief, Tan plundered heavily and withdrew.
units.literal: Before long the foreign general Shi Jiacai came from Luzhou with relief troops; Tan led the army in great plunder and returned.

units.zh: 尋授天平軍副大使，知節度使事，棄鄆、齊、曹等州觀察等使。
units.en: He was soon made deputy ambassador and acting commissioner of Tianping, with concurrent observation over Yun, Qi, and Cao.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed deputy ambassador of the Tianping army and acting military commissioner, concurrently Yun, Qi, and Cao circuit observation commissioner.

units.zh: 先是，檀招誘群盜，選其勁悍者置於帳下，以為爪牙。
units.en: Earlier he had recruited bandits and kept their fiercest men as personal guards.
units.literal: Earlier, Tan had enticed bandit bands and chose their fiercest men to place in his tent as personal guards.

units.zh: 至是，數輩竊發，突入府第，檀素不為備，遂為所害，時年五十一。
units.en: Now several of them broke into his residence unawares and killed him; he was fifty-one.
units.literal: At this time several of them rose in secret, burst into the official residence; Tan was wholly unprepared and was killed by them; he was fifty-one.

units.zh: 節度副使裴彥聞變，率府兵盡擒諸賊，州城帖然。
units.en: Deputy commissioner Pei Yan heard the alarm, seized the assassins with prefectural troops, and the city quieted.
units.literal: Deputy commissioner Pei Yan, hearing of the disturbance, led prefectural troops and seized all the bandits; the city was calm.

units.zh: 尋冊贈太師，諡曰忠毅，葬於開封縣之皋門原。
units.en: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Loyal Resolute, and buried at Gaomen in Kaifeng.
units.literal: Soon he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Loyal Resolute, and buried on the Gaomen plateau in Kaifeng county.

units.zh: 有子六人，皆升朝列。
units.en: He left six sons, all of whom entered court office.
units.literal: He had six sons, all of whom rose in court rank.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫大都偶國，《春秋》所非。
units.en: The historian writes: A great city rivaling the throne is what the 《Spring and Autumn》 condemns.
units.literal: The historian writes: A great capital rivaling the state is what the 《Spring and Autumn》 condemns.

units.zh: 當師厚之據鄴城也，綰數萬之甲兵，擅六州之輿賦，名既震主，勢亦滔天。
units.en: When Shihou held Yecheng he commanded tens of thousands of troops and the revenues of six prefectures; his fame overawed his master and his power seemed to touch the sky.
units.literal: When Shihou held Yecheng he controlled tens of thousands of armored soldiers and monopolized the levies of six prefectures; his name already alarmed his lord and his power also reached the heavens.

units.zh: 逮其喪亡，須議分割。
units.en: At his death his domains had to be carved up at once.
units.literal: When he perished, partition had to be debated at once.

units.zh: 由茲以失河朔，因是以啟晉人，《詩》所謂「誰生厲階」者，師厚之謂歟！
units.en: Thus Hebei was lost and the Jin were let in—the 《Odes》 line "who raised this mischief" surely means Shihou!
units.literal: From this Hebei was lost, and from this the Jin were invited in—the 《Odes》 phrase "who raised this mischief" surely applies to Shihou!

units.zh: 存節、王檀俱出身事主，底力圖功，觀其方略，皆將帥之良者也。
units.en: Cunjie and Wang Tan both rose in their lord's service and gave their strength to his cause; in strategy each proved an excellent commander.
units.literal: Cunjie and Wang Tan alike came forth to serve their lord and exhausted themselves in merit; viewing their strategy, both were fine generals.

units.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。
units.en: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as right regular attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。
units.en: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.
units.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
units.en: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Academy, commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and commissioner for salt and iron transport across all circuits.
units.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Academy, Commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport across all circuits.

units.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。
units.en: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made acting right vice director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.

units.zh: 太祖受禪，除右羽林統軍，尋佐劉鄩統兵收潼關，擒劉知浣獻之，乃以為右龍虎統軍兼侍衛指揮使。
units.en: At the Liang founding he was made Right Feathered Forest commander; he soon helped Liu Yan recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and commander of the palace guard.
units.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, Gui was made Right Feathered Forest commander; soon he aided Liu Yan in leading troops to recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and also commander of the palace guard.

units.zh: 及成汭敗於鄂州，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui fell at Ezhou, Kuangning had his brother Kuangming made acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated at E prefecture, Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 匡凝弟匡明，字讚堯，幼以父貴，一子出身，為江陵府文學。
units.en: His brother Kuangming, styled Zanyao, entered office young as a literary officer at Jiangling through their father's rank.
units.literal: Kuangning's younger brother Kuangming, style name Zanyao, in youth by his father's eminence entered office as a single son—he was Jiangling prefecture literary officer.

units.zh: 及建稱帝，用為大理卿、工部尚書。
units.en: When Wang Jian became emperor he made him Grand Court director and Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Jian declared himself emperor, he used him as Grand Court of Review director and Works Ministry minister.

units.zh: 及壯，以軍功曆繡、峽二州刺史。
units.en: Grown, he won military merit as inspector of Xiuxi and Xia.
units.literal: When grown, by military merit he passed through Xiuxi and Xia prefecture inspector posts.

units.zh: 天祐二年秋七月，遣楊師厚率師討之。
units.en: In autumn, month 7 of Tianyou 2, he sent Yang Shihou to attack him.
units.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn seventh month, he sent Yang Shihou to lead troops to attack him.

units.zh: 匡明亦謀奔淮南，子承規諫曰：「昔諸葛兄弟分仕二國，若適揚州，是自取疑也。」
units.en: Kuangming meant to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui warned, "Like the Zhuge brothers serving rival states, going to Yangzhou would invite suspicion."
units.literal: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui remonstrated: "In old times the Zhuge brothers each served a different state—if you go to Yangzhou, it is yourself inviting suspicion."

units.zh: 成汭之敗，其兄匡凝表為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui's defeat his brother made him acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated, his elder brother Kuangning memorialized him as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 久之，卒於蜀。
units.en: He died in Shu many years later.
units.literal: After long time he died in Shu.

units.zh: 匡明謂然，乃趨成都。
units.en: Kuangming agreed and fled to Chengdu instead.
units.literal: Kuangming thought it so and thereupon hastened to Chengdu.

units.zh: 匡明領兵逐之，遂鎮於渚宮。
units.en: Kuangming drove them off and held court at Zhugong.
units.literal: Kuangming led troops to drive them off and then held commission at Zhugong.

units.zh: 匡明懼，乃舉族上峽奔蜀，王建待以賓禮。
units.en: Kuangming fled upriver to Shu with his clan; Wang Jian received him as an honored guest.
units.literal: Kuangming feared and thereupon led his clan up the gorge to flee to Shu; Wang Jian received him with guest ceremony.

units.zh: 帝不忍，以浮代賈復為執金吾，徙封父城侯。
units.en: The emperor spared him: Zhu Fu succeeded Jia Fu as Bearer of the Golden Mace and was transferred to the marquisate of Fucheng.
units.literal: The emperor could not bear it; he replaced Jia Fu with Fu as Bearer of the Mace and transferred his fief to marquis of Fucheng.

units.zh: 明年，涿郡太守張豐亦舉兵反。
units.en: The following year Zhang Feng, governor of Zhuojun, rose in rebellion as well.
units.literal: The next year the governor of Zhuojun Zhang Feng also raised troops and rebelled.

units.zh: 貞明六年春正月戊子，以曹州刺史朱漢賓為安州宣威軍節度使；
units.en: On wuzi in the first month of Zhenming 6, Zhu Hanbin, prefect of Cao, was appointed military commissioner of the Xuanwei Army at An.
units.literal: On wuzi, first month of spring of Zhenming 6, Cao prefect Zhu Hanbin was made Anzhou Xuanwei Army military commissioner;

units.zh: 趙匡凝，
units.en: Next was Zhao Kuangning,
units.literal: Zhao Kuangning,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：匡凝字光儀。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 gives his style as Guangyi.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Kuangning's style name was Guangyi.)〉

units.zh: 及德諲卒，匡凝自為襄州留後，朝廷即以旄鉞授之。
units.en: When Dexin died Kuangning made himself acting commissioner and received the court commission.
units.literal: When Dexin died, Kuangning made himself Xiangzhou acting commissioner; the court thereupon bestowed the command baton and axe.

units.zh: 匡凝以父功為唐州刺史兼七州馬步軍都校。
units.en: Kuangning became Tang prefect inspector and overall commander of seven prefectures' horse and foot through his father's merit.
units.literal: Kuangning by his father's merit was Tang prefecture inspector and concurrent seven-prefecture horse-and-foot army overall commander.

units.zh: 唐光啟四年夏六月，德諲審宗權必敗，乃舉漢南之地以歸唐朝，仍遣使投分於太祖，兼誓戮力，同討宗權。
units.en: In summer, month 6 of Guangqi 4, Dexin saw Zongquan would fall, surrendered Hannan to Tang, sent envoys to the Founder, and swore to destroy Zongquan together.
units.literal: Tang Guangqi year 4 summer sixth month, Dexin judged Zongquan would surely be defeated and thereupon raised the Hannan lands to return to Tang, still sending envoys to declare separation to the Founder and jointly swearing united strength to attack Zongquan together.

units.zh: 蔡州人也。
units.en: was a native of Cai prefecture.
units.literal: was a man of Cai prefecture.

units.zh: 匡凝氣貌甚偉，好自修飾，每整衣冠，必使人持巨鑒前後照之。
units.en: Tall and vain, he had great mirrors held before and behind him whenever he dressed.
units.literal: Kuangning's bearing was very grand; he loved self-adornment—each time he arranged cap and robes he must have men hold great mirrors before and behind to shine on him.

units.zh: 對客之際，烏巾上微覺有塵，即令侍妓持紅拂以去之。
units.en: If he sensed dust on his black cap before guests, maids brushed it away with red dusters.
units.literal: When facing guests, on the black cap he slightly sensed dust and at once ordered serving girls to hold red dusters to remove it.

units.zh: 八月，太祖親領大軍南征，仍請削匡凝在身官爵。
units.en: Month 8 the Founder marched south in person and had Kuangning stripped of rank.
units.literal: Eighth month, the Founder personally led a great army south on campaign and still requested stripping Kuangning of his personal offices and titles.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：行密厚遇匡凝，其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。
units.en: Ouyang's 《History》 says Xingmi treated Kuangning well, but after Xingmi's death Yang Wo grew rude to him.
units.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》 says: Xingmi treated Kuangning generously; afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo gradually was without courtesy to him.

units.zh: 諸將以為慢，渥遣匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。）〉
units.en: Officers took it as insult; Wo exiled him to Hailing, where Xu Wen later killed him.)〉
units.literal: The generals thought it disrespect; Wo sent Kuangning to Hailing and later Xu Wen killed him.)〉

units.zh: 初，匡凝好聚書，及敗，楊師厚獲數千卷於第，悉以來獻。
units.en: Kuangning had loved books; after his defeat Shihou seized thousands of scrolls from his house and presented them to the Founder.
units.literal: At first Kuangning loved gathering books; when defeated, Yang Shihou obtained several thousand scrolls at his residence and entirely brought them as tribute.

units.zh: 匡凝對使者流涕，答以受國恩深，豈敢隨時妄有他誌。
units.en: Kuangning wept before the envoy and said the state's grace was too deep for him to change sides with the times.
units.literal: Kuangning to the envoy wept and replied that the state's grace was deep—how dare he follow the times and rashly have another intent.

units.zh: 渥方宴食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。」
units.en: At a feast Wo ate green plums; Kuangning warned, "Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children."
units.literal: Wo was just feasting and eating green plums; Kuangning looked at Wo and said: "Do not eat much—it brings children's fever."

units.zh: 光化初，匡凝以太祖有清口之敗，密附於淮夷，太祖遣氏叔琮率師伐之。
units.en: Early in Guanghua, after the Founder's defeat at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly sided with the Huai rebels and the Founder sent Shi Shucong against him.
units.literal: At the start of Guanghua, because the Founder had been defeated at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly attached himself to the Huai forces; the Founder sent Shi Shucong with troops to attack him.

units.zh: 俄而康懷英攻下鄧州，匡凝懼，遣使乞盟，太祖許之，自是附庸於太祖。
units.en: Kang Huaiying took Deng; Kuangning sued for peace, the Founder agreed, and he became a vassal.
units.literal: Soon Kang Huaiying attacked and took Deng prefecture; Kuangning feared and sent envoys to beg alliance—the Founder permitted it; from then he was a vassal of the Founder.

units.zh: 是時唐室微弱，諸道常賦多不上供，惟匡凝昆仲雖強據江山，然盡忠帝室，貢賦不絕。
units.en: While Tang weakened and most circuits withheld tribute, the Zhao brothers still sent loyal levies from their strongholds.
units.literal: At that time the Tang house was weak; many circuits' regular levies often did not go up in tribute—only Kuangning and his brothers, though strongly holding rivers and mountains, yet were wholly loyal to the imperial house and tribute and levies did not cease.

units.zh: 太祖將期受禪，以匡凝兄弟並據藩鎮，乃遣使先諭旨焉。
units.en: As the Founder prepared to take the throne, he sent envoys ahead to the Zhao brothers holding the frontier commands.
units.literal: The Founder was about to fix the date to receive the abdication mandate; because Kuangning and his brothers both held frontier commissions, he sent envoys first to announce the intent.

units.zh: 及師厚濟江，匡凝以兵數萬逆戰，大為師厚所敗，匡凝乃燔其舟，單舸急棹，沿漢而遁於金陵。
units.en: Shihou crossed the river; Kuangning met him with tens of thousands, was routed, burned his fleet, and fled alone up the Han to Jinling.
units.literal: When Shihou crossed the river, Kuangning with tens of thousands of troops met him in battle and was greatly defeated by Shihou; Kuangning then burned his boats, in a single skiff urgently rowed, and along the Han fled to Jinling.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：師厚由陰穀伐木為梁，匡凝以兵二萬瀕江戰，大敗，乃燔州，單舸夜奔揚州。
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou bridged Yin Valley, Kuangning lost twenty thousand along the river, burned the prefecture, and fled by night to Yangzhou.
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou by Yin Valley felled timber for beams; Kuangning with twenty thousand troops fought along the river, was greatly defeated, then burned the prefecture and in a single skiff fled by night to Yangzhou.

units.zh: 從朱珍討徐州，撥豐縣，敗時溥於吳康，得其輜重，加檢校刑部尚書。
units.en: At Xuzhou he took Feng, beat Shi Pu at Wukang, and became honorary Minister of Punishments.
units.literal: Following Zhu Zhen to attack Xuzhou he took Feng county, defeated Shi Pu at Wukang, obtained his baggage train, and was added honorary Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 及佐朱珍討時溥，寨於豐、蕭之間，歸厚乘徐壘如行坦途，甚為諸將歎伏。
units.en: Besieging Shi Pu he crossed Xu walls as if on flat ground.
units.literal: When aiding Zhu Zhen against Shi Pu he stockaded between Feng and Xiao; Guihou crossed Xu ramparts as if on level road—generals deeply sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。
units.en: During Huang Chao's rebellion, Zhuge Shuang accepted a bogus appointment from him as military governor of Heyang.
units.literal: During the rebellion of the bandit Huang Chao, Zhuge Shuang received from him a false appointment as military governor of Heyang.

units.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。
units.en: The emperor was then in Shu while rebels swarmed the land. Jian held six prefectures and a powerful army; nursing secret ambitions of rebellion and eager to enlarge his domain, he marched on Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
units.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and robbers swarmed forth. Jian held six prefectures, his armor and troops were strong, and he secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation and wished to expand his territory; he therefore raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。
units.en: Jian besieged the city for half a year without success, while Heyang was seized again by Zhuge Shuang.
units.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized by Zhuge Shuang.

units.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。
units.en: He captured Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang from the field.
units.literal: He took Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang to flight.

units.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。
units.en: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxiang, Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
units.literal: Soon he shifted his army to attack Heyang again; when he reached Xinxing he was struck in counterattack by Shuang's army and defeated.
